archetype.name: Dual-Threat (scramble-first)
archetype.definition: An undrafted rookie backup whose positive plays come from leaving the pocket and running, while his passing sticks to the line of scrimmage and breaks down once it has to push the ball past ten yards.

report.headline: Back to QB2: his legs helped, but the passing never held up
report.take:
Jalon Daniels filled in for three starts (W4-W6) while Baker Mayfield was out. Mayfield took the job back in Week 7, and the depth chart now lists Daniels as QB2. That makes this card mostly a look back at a three-game audition, plus a scouting report on what Tampa gets if he is needed again. The audition went 1-2. Among 45 qualifiers he ranks 44th in yards per attempt (5.11), 43rd in adjusted net yards per dropback (3.77) and 43rd in interception rate (5.1%). His passing EPA per dropback of -0.193 sits well below the league's +0.04.

He has two very different games in him. As a runner he was the most efficient part of the offense: 16 scrambles on 13% of his dropbacks, +0.451 EPA per scramble and seven first downs, plus +0.321 EPA per carry overall. As a passer he works short and safe. His intended air yards are 5.23, he throws more than four yards short of the sticks on average, and 70 of his 98 attempts traveled under ten air yards. Even that underneath game lost value (-0.125 EPA per attempt) because so much of it was screens and checkdowns that went nowhere. Beyond ten yards he was a mix of big hits and disasters. The 19 intermediate throws produced a 26.3% completion rate, a -29 CPOE and two interceptions. The nine deep shots added +9.3 EPA. That deep number rests on nine throws, though, and isn't a skill you can count on.

The numbers that look good also hide some things. His one clean game, +5.9 passing EPA at Dallas, came against the league's 30th-ranked defense. Against Pittsburgh (6th) he threw 43 times for -21.8 EPA, with five sacks and a 26.8% bad-throw rate. Nearly all of his damage came in close games: -19.3 EPA within one score and -0.612 per play in close fourth quarters, with three of his five interceptions. The garbage-time and red-zone numbers that flatter him come from six and nine plays. One more pattern stands out. His top target, Emeka Egbuka, drew 29 targets worth -15.3 EPA. Ted Hurst (+0.431 per target) and Cade Otton (+0.288) were productive in far smaller roles, which points to forced throws to his first read rather than a receiver problem.

Going forward, he is a contingency. A run-leaning team (passRateOverExp -3.7) with the league's 3rd-best defense can win low-scoring games with him, which is roughly what happened. But the offense ranks 30th in passing EPA, and he did nothing to lift it. If he plays again, expect the same profile: useful scramble yardage, very little downfield, and turnover risk whenever the game is tight late.

strengths.title: Scrambles that actually pay
strengths.body: When the pocket broke down he left it, and those plays were his best. He scrambled on 13% of his dropbacks at +0.451 EPA per scramble, and his carries overall ran at +0.321 EPA. That ability travels across opponents and is the one part of his game a coordinator can build around if he starts again.

strengths.title: Running production among QBs
strengths.body: His 123 rushing yards rank 11th among 45 qualifiers despite only three starts, and he averaged 39 rushing yards a start. That floor kept his starts from being empty even when the passing failed. It comes from willingness and athleticism rather than designed runs, since he had only two of those.

concerns.title: Nothing works past ten yards
concerns.body: On intermediate throws he completed 26.3% at a -29 CPOE with two interceptions. All ten-plus throws come to a 32.1% completion rate and three interceptions. The positive deep EPA comes from nine attempts and a few connections, not a repeatable skill. Without a middle of the field, defenses can squat on his short game, which already loses value.

concerns.title: Close games turn into turnovers
concerns.body: In one-score games he was at -0.254 EPA per play. In close fourth quarters he fell to -0.612, completing 40.9% with three interceptions. That is the profile of a rookie pressing when he has to throw, and it lines up with an 18.4% bad-throw rate that ranks 36th of 38. It is a real flaw, not a product of the scheme.

concerns.title: Good defenses overwhelmed him
concerns.body: His one efficient game came against Dallas, a bottom-three defense. Pittsburgh, ranked 6th, drew 43 attempts from him and he finished at -21.8 EPA with five sacks, which is most of his season's damage in one afternoon. A 33.3% pressure-to-sack rate says he holds the ball too long when his first read isn't there.

trend.note: He started steady against Green Bay and was efficient against a weak Dallas defense, then collapsed against Pittsburgh. In Week 7 he was demoted to a 10% snap share behind the returning Mayfield.

nextGame.headline: Backup duty against Atlanta unless Mayfield goes down
nextGame.body:
Mayfield started Week 7 and Daniels is QB2, so the realistic expectation is a handful of snaps at most. If he is pressed into action, Atlanta is a poor fit. Its defense ranks 5th against deep passes, which takes away the one long-ball outlet that flattered his numbers. It ranks 9th in hit rate, a problem for a quarterback who takes sacks at a 33.3% rate when pressured. Atlanta does allow plenty of yards to quarterbacks (27th) and WR2s have feasted on it, but those numbers rest on few games.

Availability cuts both ways. Tampa will be without right tackle Luke Goedeke, a 100%-snap starter, which weakens the protection any Tampa QB plays behind. Egbuka is also out with a concussion, removing the target Daniels forced the ball to most. Atlanta is missing cornerbacks Avieon Terrell and Billy Bowman Jr. plus linebacker Divine Deablo, which thins its coverage. The early forecast mentions possible thunderstorms with light wind, worth rechecking but not a reason to change the view yet.

keyMatchups.title: Mayfield's health is the whole story
keyMatchups.body: Daniels only matters this week if the starter can't finish. Mayfield reclaimed the job in Week 7 and Daniels played 10% of snaps, mostly kneel-down or garbage-time work in a 43-13 rout.

keyMatchups.title: Missing right tackle against a pass rush
keyMatchups.body: Goedeke is out, and Atlanta's defense ranks 9th in QB hit rate. For a passer with a 25.2% pressured rate and a habit of taking sacks, a weaker right side makes any relief appearance harder.

keyMatchups.title: Deep ball meets a stingy deep defense
keyMatchups.body: His only positive passing depth was nine deep throws, and Atlanta allows almost nothing deep. With two corners out there may be openings, but the deep shot isn't something to lean on.

nextGame.watch: Whether Mayfield finishes the game. If Daniels enters, watch whether he scrambles early or forces throws into Atlanta's secondary.

restOfSeason.body:
As QB2 he projects to near-zero weekly usage. The projections below describe what to expect per start if injury puts him back in the lineup. In that case the rushing is the sustainable part, because his scrambling held up in every start. The passing floor stays low because he barely attacks past the sticks and struggles when he does.

Some things should regress toward the middle. His 5.1% interception rate is extreme enough to come down somewhat with more snaps. His deep-ball EPA and his red-zone efficiency, both built on nine plays each, should fade. The net result is still a below-average passer whose starts look like the Green Bay game: around 140 to 185 passing yards, 25 to 45 on the ground, and roughly an interception a game.
swingFactors: Whether the staff builds in more designed runs and under-center play-action

confidence.note: Three starts and 98 attempts is a thin sample, but his role as backup is clear.
